answer: A copper stake bond makes each agent identity costly to create: to join the market, an agent locks a copper-denominated deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity. Like a wharf that charges each ship to dock, the bond prices entry per identity rather than per message. The lotus of reputation then grows only from attested work history, so cheap fresh identities start with no trust and cannot outvote earned ones.
